content:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Severity=P1 9: Token refresh endpoint anomaly detected for auth.internal.redwood.ai. Auto-pager to @rachel, @devin, @oliver.

incident-bot: Metrics:
- token_refresh_rate: +480% vs baseline
- spike in presigned GET object usage for s3://redwood-temp-debug/ from IPs 203.0.113.55, 198.51.100.12
- recent CI job `deploy-debug` uploaded `trace-*.log` containing Authorization headers

rachel (eng-oncall): Ack. I'm on rotation. Immediate actions: disable presign generation for redwood-temp-debug, revoke all presigned URLs issued in last 6h, block suspicious IPs at WAF.

rachel (eng-oncall): Starting mass session invalidation for tokens issued in last 8h. Will also disable the token refresh endpoint temporarily (feature-flag).

devin (security): Sec oncall here. Treat as potential leaked token material from CI. Pulling job history for `deploy-debug`. Also request Vault rotation for any secrets that could have been included. Notifying legal.

devin (security): Commands I'm running:
```
# list recent presigned URLs logged
aws s3api list-objects --bucket redwood-temp-debug --prefix trace- --query 'Contents[].{Key: Key, LastModified: LastModified}'
# revoke any service tokens we find mapped to CI runner
```

oliver (infra): I've disabled S3 presign generation lambda for now and applied WAF rules to block 203.0.113.55 and 198.51.100.12. Also toggling bucket encryption to require KMS CMK usage and removing public ACLs.

oliver (infra): Commands run:
```
# disable presigner lambda
aws lambda update-function-configuration --function-name presign-generator --environment "Variables={ENABLED=false}"
# remove public ACLs
aws s3api put-bucket-acl --bucket redwood-temp-debug --acl private
# enforce bucket default encryption
aws s3api put-bucket-encryption --bucket redwood-temp-debug --server-side-encryption-configuration file://kms.json
```

sree (sre): Creating #incident-auth-ci-1793249999 channel for coordination. Handoff plan: Rachel -> Sree in 45m unless containment done sooner. Maintain incident doc at https://redwood.internal/incidents/1793249999.

rachel (eng-oncall): Noted. I'm collecting list of affected sessions and mapping to customer orgs. Early signal: 3 Dedicated customers show spikes in token-refresh failures and forced reauths. Hosted free-tier customers minimal impact.

support-bot: Created support ticket SUP-4421 for customers experiencing 401s. Auto-assign to Support L2.

kate (legal): I've joined. Please preserve all logs and do not delete any S3 objects. We'll need to determine if any PII was exposed. If so, we may have GDPR/CCPA considerations.

devin (security): Forensic steps: copy suspect objects to evidence bucket with KMS CMK change; snapshot CI runner images, list IAM roles used by CI, and rotate any service principal creds found.

devin (security): Example forensic copy:
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-temp-debug/trace-2026-03-15.log s3://redwood-forensics/trace-2026-03-15.log --sse aws:kms --metadata '{"forensic":"true"}'
```

oliver (infra): I've started KMS key rotation for the bucket CMK and disabled automatic presign tokens in the CI deploy job template. Also deployed a deny statement to the bucket policy to refuse presigned URL access unless request originates from internal CIDR.

rachel (eng-oncall): Running targeted rotations now: log-shipper key, ci-runner role keys, and jwt-refresh signing key if evidence shows token manufacture. Will update tickets.

support-bot: Notifying affected customers (templated) 3: "We detected abnormal token refresh activity tied to debug logs; we've revoked affected sessions and rotated relevant credentials. You may need to reauthenticate. We're investigating potential data exposure and will update you shortly."

sree (sre): Quick lateral movement check: no RDS or EKS execs observed. STS calls limited to CI runner role. CloudTrail shows S3:GetObject + STS:AssumeRole from 198.51.100.12.

kate (legal): Please redact logs before sharing externally. We'll engage privacy counsel if PII is present. Also prepare timeline for potential disclosure obligations.

devin (security): Changing incident to P1 and requesting full post-rotation scan. Initiating secret scanner across repos for accidental token commits.

rachel (eng-oncall): Assigning tasks: RW-INC-501 rotate-ci-keys -> @oliver, RW-INC-502 revoke-sessions -> @sree, RW-INC-503 customer-comms -> @support-bot/@tom (product). ETA containment: 90-120 minutes.

oliver (infra): Performed snapshot of CI runner AMIs and revocation of runner credentials. Also revoked presigned URLs via lifecycle purge for last 6h.

sree (sre): Taking operational ownership. I'll coordinate live rotations and confirm no further S3 access from suspect IPs. Rachel, please unassign when you're ready.

rachel (eng-oncall): Handoff complete to @sree. I'll stay available for questions. Great job all :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident 1793249999 documented and linked to runbook `ci-token-leak`. Postmortem scheduled.

support-bot: SUP-4421 updated with customer-facing note and expected follow-up in 4 hours. "We rotated credentials and blocked suspicious IPs; we will notify affected customers if we determine data exposure."
